title: Faxanadu
subtitle: A troubled homecoming

body: Faxanadu is a side-scrolling action role-playing game developed by Hudson Soft for the NES. A traveller returns to Eolis to find an almost deserted town: its water supply has failed and hostile dwarves threaten the elves. The king sends him out with a little gold and a large problem. Towns, passages and dungeons form a connected journey in which the next purchase can matter as much as the next sword fight. The name joins Famicom and Xanadu, although Hudson built a distinct adventure around Falcom’s licence.

The hero walks, jumps and climbs through spaces occupied by enemies, ladders and narrow platforms. A sword handles nearby threats while magic provides a way to strike from a distance. Defeated creatures can leave money or bread, linking survival to the economy of the journey. Shops sell equipment and useful supplies, so returning to a settlement gives exploration a practical rhythm. Each departure asks the player to judge whether the current weapon, armour and remaining resources are enough for the route ahead.

Progress also has a place in the world. Gurus offer passwords called mantras, allowing the adventure to continue later without a battery save. Experience raises the hero’s rank, while money and equipment provide more immediate improvements. These systems give the journey two scales: the individual jump or encounter and the longer preparation for an unfamiliar area. Faxanadu’s appeal lies in that combination. Reaching a town feels like an arrival because the road has demanded attention, and leaving it means carrying a new set of possibilities.
